title: Check disk and CPU activity on Mac
summary: Use the iostat command in Terminal to see how much your disk and CPU are working. It shows transfer speeds, CPU usage percentages, and system load averages.

steps.explain: Run iostat to get a snapshot of device statistics (transfer rates), CPU statistics (user, system, idle percentages), and system load averages.
steps.expect: A table showing disk transfer rates (KB/t, tps, MB/s), CPU percentages (%us, %sy, %id), and load averages (1, 5, 15 min).

steps.explain: If you want to monitor changes over time, run iostat with an interval (in seconds) to see incremental reports.
steps.expect: A continuous stream of statistics updating every 2 seconds. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

alternatives.explain: Monitor a specific disk (e.g., disk0) every second.

placeholders.name: DISK
placeholders.description: The disk identifier, e.g., disk0 or disk1
